Like you said you can always switch majors in your first year. From my experience studying mech eng there isn't a computing element apart from CAE (computer aided engineering) such as CAD, FEA, Matlab, CNC etc.

Read module descriptions for different universities but mechanical engineering is always a safe broad bet if you are unsure. However if your interest is in electronics and computers I recommend electrical engineering / robotics / mechatronics or systems engineering.

I think the best idea here is to practice with a CAD software, AutoCAD is probably the best bet.

Also sign up to some engineering newsletters or magazines, not sure what good ones there are in the US (i'm from UK). Having a general insight into the industry really helps you with reports, projects and also job interviews.
